solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Volunteers to carry pen for one African native (6)

indicators.note: the outer piece holds the inner one, as a bearer carries a load

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a pen is a female swan; 'for one' marks it as an example

annotation.surface: Volunteers helping to carry a pen for an African man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool; it is a female swan. The Tswana are a people of Botswana and South Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: A Tswana is a native of Botswana and neighbouring southern Africa.

entries.clue: Tree ring not quite in profusion (7)

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its last letter
the shortened ring goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a sea of faces is a profusion of them
QUOIT, a ring tossed in a game, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A tree ring that almost appears in abundance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tree ring' reads as one thing, a growth ring; split them, and the ring is a quoit, the rope or iron hoop thrown at a peg.
annotation.definitionFit: The sequoia is the giant redwood of California.

blocks.note: as printed
gent is short for gentleman, a man or chap

annotation.surface: Describing someone as one more spy.
annotation.walkthrough: A plain charade: the article stays as it is and the fellow is a gentleman, shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a secret agent is one who spies for a government.

entries.clue: Concrete walling a flooded valley – risky? (9)

definitions.note: the definition is by example: actuarial work is the calculation of risk

indicators.note: the outer word builds a wall around the inner

blocks.note: concrete as in real, actual
a ria is a river valley drowned by the sea; the 'a' is just the article

annotation.surface: An engineer wondering whether a concrete dam around a flooded valley is dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' plays the building material but is the adjective meaning real. The question mark flags the loose definition: actuarial is 'to do with risk', not 'risky'.
annotation.definitionFit: Actuaries price risk, so actuarial matters are matters of risk.

entries.clue: Bear hugs are left over for bear (8)

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run backwards
the outer word wraps its arms round the inner

blocks.note: to bear a load is to tote it
ARE + L (left), turned over

annotation.surface: Bear hugs that are left over for a bear, like leftovers at a zoo.
annotation.walkthrough: The two bears do different jobs: the first is 'carry' and the second is 'put up with'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what you can bear you put up with, as in 'I can't bear noise'.

entries.clue: Approaching 40 mph, losing power is right, yet not prepared (6-9)

indicators.note: mph is losing something: the P for power drops out of it
the letters are made up into something new

blocks.note: MPH without P (power)
anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A driver creeping up towards 40 mph and losing power, not ready for it.
annotation.walkthrough: The 40 and the mph look like one speed; the 40 belongs to the definition, an age, and the mph is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone thirty-something is in their thirties, heading towards 40.

indicators.note: the good, G, is taken out

blocks.note: to linger is to delay
standard abbreviation, removed

annotation.surface: Complaining that a ship's delay is bad news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delay' is the verb, to hang about; 'not good' then takes the G away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a liner is an ocean-going passenger ship running a regular line.

indicators.note: the second piece is added to the first

blocks.note: rounds of ammunition
to man a ship is to crew it

annotation.surface: Someone who delivers ammunition to a ship's crew.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like a noun receiving the ammunition; it is the verb. A roundsman is a British delivery man on a regular route, like a milkman.
annotation.definitionFit: A roundsman delivers goods such as milk or bread along a round.

entries.clue: Order parts for Parisian from market (5,2)

indicators.note: the outer word splits open to make room for the inner

blocks.note: a train of events is an ordered sequence
French for 'from'

annotation.surface: Ordering parts for a Parisian from a market stall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like an instruction to buy; it is TRAIN. 'Market' is a verb: to trade in goods is to deal in them.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a firm that trades in something buys and sells it, which is what marketing goods means.

entries.clue: Rider in hunt cutting a rein to pieces (10)

indicators.note: the word slices into the middle of the other letters
the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: a quest is a hunt
A REIN rearranged, with QUEST cutting in after the E

annotation.surface: A huntsman slashing through a rein until it falls apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all horse gear, so 'hunt' reads as the fox hunt; it is simply QUEST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Latin equus, horse: an equestrian is a horseman or horsewoman.

entries.clue: State area in heart of Monmouthshire (4)

indicators.note: A is placed in the heart letters, sitting between UT and H
the central letters of the word

blocks.note: the middle three of monmoUTHshire
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A patch of land at the centre of Monmouthshire, a Welsh county.
annotation.walkthrough: The Welsh county points away from America, but the state is a US one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Utah is one of the fifty United States.

blocks.note: you contract an illness when you get it
to bridge a river is to cross it

annotation.surface: A game that makes the players angry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' plays the adjective, annoyed; it is the verb, as in crossing a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard form of the card game bridge.

blocks.note: familiar word for mother
steamship, as in SS Great Britain

annotation.surface: A mother ship serving in the navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mother ship' reads as one naval term, the vessel that supplies smaller craft. 'Service' is a church service.
annotation.definitionFit: Mass is the Catholic church service of the Eucharist.

indicators.note: the letters flow into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A rival shop boasting it also stocks a liquid scouring agent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liquid abrasive' reads as a product, a liquid cleaner; 'liquid' is the anagram indicator, and steel wool is anything but liquid.
annotation.definitionFit: Steel wool is a mass of fine steel threads used for scouring.

indicators.note: the men prise the bar open and sit inside it

blocks.note: in fashion
a strut is a supporting bar
guys are men

annotation.surface: Staff from an agency opening a fashionable bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trendy bar' reads as a nightspot; the bar is a strut, a piece of framework.
annotation.definitionFit: An instrument is the means or agency by which something is done.

indicators.note: the letters are set loose to regroup

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A traveller asking whether coming back into Britain costs anything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enter' plays the verb; it is the keyboard key, the one also called Return.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in keyboard terms: the key marked Enter on a PC is labelled Return on many other keyboards.

entries.clue: If you step on it you may break it (5,5)

definitions.text: If you step on it you may break it

blocks.note: read as treading on something, and meant as the driver's slang for putting your foot down on the accelerator
read as snapping something underfoot, and meant as breaking a rule by going too fast

annotation.surface: A warning about treading on something fragile.
annotation.walkthrough: The two 'it's look like the same fragile object; the first is the accelerator pedal, the second the legal maximum you exceed by pressing it.
annotation.definitionFit: A speed limit is what motorists break when they step on it, driving faster than the law allows.

entries.clue: It is put in lasagna, say (7)

definitions.text: It is put in lasagna, say

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second
lasagna is one example of the wider class

blocks.note: 'it' is sex appeal, SA
lasagna is a kind of pasta

annotation.surface: A recipe note: this goes into lasagna.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: SA put in PASTA, and the answer is a thing put in lasagna.
annotation.definitionFit: Passata, sieved tomato, is a standard ingredient of lasagna.

entries.clue: Arkwright leads in new Open All Hours (4)

indicators.note: the leading letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of New Open All Hours

annotation.surface: Arkwright, the shopkeeper in the BBC sitcom Open All Hours, starring in a new version.
annotation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like the sitcom character; it is split as ark + wright, a builder of the ark.
annotation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark, so he was an ark-wright.

indicators.note: the letters take off and land in a new order
the word doubles as its own instruction, setting itself in the middle of the rearranged dream

blocks.note: DREAM rearranged, opened after AMER
as printed, placed inside

annotation.surface: Dreaming of a crow in flight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crow' is the bird in the surface; with a capital it is the Crow people of Montana. The capital cannot be trusted as a signal, since first words are always capitalised.
annotation.definitionFit: The Crow are a Native American people, and Amerind means an American Indian.

entries.clue: Others may not be so far from altruistic (4-10)

definitions.text: Others may not be so far from altruistic

blocks.note: read as a comparison with other people, and meant literally: others may not be interested in your self
the straight meaning, a person who puts their own interests first

annotation.surface: A remark that other people may be less selfless than you.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'so' as 'interested in (you)', which others may well not be; the second half then gives the ordinary sense of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone self-interested looks after number one, the opposite of altruism, which puts others first.

blocks.note: the verb, to put a body in a grave
the Milan club Internazionale, of Serie A

annotation.surface: Bury FC, an English football club, somehow playing in Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester with its own football club, so 'Bury FC' reads as one name; the verb and the Italian club are separate.
annotation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, and Inter is the Milan football club.

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the next words

blocks.note: houSE GUEsts

annotation.surface: Guests moving smoothly from one room of a house to the next.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words, starting in the tail of 'house'.
annotation.definitionFit: A segue is a smooth move from one thing to the next.

blocks.note: can in the sense of being allowed, may
as in o'clock, short for 'of the clock'

annotation.surface: A tin of sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can of' looks like a container; 'can' is the verb (may) and 'of' shrinks to O.
annotation.definitionFit: A casual abbreviation: mayo is everyday shorthand for mayonnaise, the egg-and-oil sauce.

entries.clue: I wouldn’t dilute spirit having put on weight (5,5)

blocks.note: to thin a liquid is to dilute it
the ka is the spirit or soul in ancient Egyptian belief
to put on weight is to gain

annotation.surface: A drinker refusing to water down spirits after gaining weight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests gin or whisky; here it is KA. The definition is a warning phrase: 'I wouldn't (do that)' means 'think again'.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying 'I wouldn't' warns someone off, as does 'think again'.

indicators.note: the boast goes around the partner

blocks.note: to brag is to boast
an ally is a partner

annotation.surface: Hector, the Trojan hero, bragging about his comrade.
annotation.walkthrough: Hector looks like the Trojan prince; it is the verb hector, to bully.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ballyrag is a variant of bullyrag, to bully, which is what hectoring someone is.

blocks.note: to yield is to give in
as a verb, to produce as a return, the way an investment does

annotation.surface: Someone surrendering in exchange for something.
annotation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one phrase, 'gives in return'; split them after 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: Yields means both gives in and (as a noun) returns on money.
